company: TPG Internet Pty Ltd / TPG Telecom Limited (ASX:TPG)
source_passage: Telco/ISP holding large volumes of customer PII, with TWO confirmed high-severity breaches: the iiNet order-management breach (identified 16 Aug 2025, disclosed to ASX 19 Aug 2025) exfiltrating ~280,000 active customer email addresses plus landlines, addresses and ~1,700 modem passwords via stolen employee credentials; and the Dec 2022 Hosted Exchange breach affecting up to ~15,000 iiNet/Westnet business customers (identified by Mandiant). Recency (a 2025 incident), severity, the high-data-sensitivity telco sector and group scale make this the single most amenable target. The breaches were notified under the OAIC NDB scheme and worked with ACSC/NOCS. iiNet (TPG brand) Aug 2025 breach: ~280k customer emails, ~20k landlines, ~10k usernames+addresses, ~1,700 modem passwords via stolen employee credentials; OAIC/ACSC engaged Dec 2022 Hosted Exchange breach affecting up to ~15k iiNet/Westnet business email customers; Mandiant identified the unauthorised access (attacker hunting crypto/financial data) Historical regulator scrutiny: ACCC s.87B undertaking against TPG Internet Pty Ltd over misleading FTTN/FTTB broadband speed claims (non-cyber) Parent: TPG Telecom Limited (ASX:TPG), formed by 2020 TPG + Vodafone Hutchison Australia merger Substantial shareholders: CK Hutchison/Hutchison Telecommunications Australia (~23.98%), Vodafone Group plc (~23.98%), Washington H. Soul Pattinson (~12.78%) Sibling brands: iiNet, Internode, Westnet, AAPT, Lebara, felix, Vodafone (iiNet/Westnet are the breached brands) Technology supplier: Ericsson (2023 AI network analytics deal) Incident-response adviser: Mandiant (Google) Competitors: Telstra, Optus (Optus is also a MOCN network-sharing partner) External auditor of parent: KPMG
